posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
What would be interesting in my opinion would be to weakly pre-expose a DCG layer to short wavelength light - possibly to some small UV lamp or even a photographic flash. Then have a look at the absorption spectrum.

The idea behind would be to verify the assumption of that French research group (Bolte et al.) that upon 380nm - blue exposure the Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(V) which was said to be relatively stable and to show an absorption peak around 520nm.

Perhaps that kind of pre-exposing DCG to UV-blue might actually speed up green sensitivity of the system also.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
Hey Tony, Martin has a good idea here. We were already talking about UV lamps, and it should be an easy experiment to try. Just take a normal DCG layer, cover half of it, expose that half to UV light, then check the absorption of each side.

For a long time now, many of us on this forum have been wondering why DCG is somewhat sensitive to 532, when the absorption spectrum suggests that it shouldn't have any sensitivity at all. (Those discussions led to the development of G307.) As a matter of fact, holograms can even be formed at 633, but the exposure times are impractically long.

Martin, could you tell me which paper states that CrV has an absorption peak around 520?

at all just as bumble bees should not in theory be able to fly .

However the explanation of why it works is quite mundane really and it does not involve anything to do with the alluring idea that the transitory CrV formation makes a longer wavelength absorption.

We have been misled by judging the total absorption spectrum of dichromate from 350nm to 650nm.

Instead the spectrum of a gelatin with a **high concentration**of dichromate should be run only from say 510nm to 650nm. 

It is simply that we get sensitivity to 532nm by using such a very high concentration . We also have discussed here getting a still higher 

sensitivity by using the incredibly soluble salt sodium dichromate instead of the potassium salt this assumes that this will enable us to pack in still more

Jeff
